definitions.explanation: Poetry written in classical Chinese, including works by Chinese poets and poems composed in classical Chinese by Japanese poets. A major literary tradition studied in Japanese education.

examples.japanese: {漢詩|かんし}を{暗唱|あんしょう}する。
examples.english: I recite Chinese poetry from memory.

examples.japanese: {高校|こうこう}の{国語|こくご}で{漢詩|かんし}を{習|なら}った。
examples.english: I studied Chinese poetry in high school Japanese class.

examples.japanese: {李白|りはく}や{杜甫|とほ}の{漢詩|かんし}は{日本|にほん}でも{広|ひろ}く{親|した}しまれている。
examples.english: The Chinese poetry of Li Bai and Du Fu is widely appreciated in Japan as well.

notes:
USAGE:
{漢詩|かんし} is part of the Japanese school curriculum and is studied in {国語|こくご} (Japanese language) class, not as a foreign language. Classical Chinese poems are read using {訓読|くんどく}み (Japanese reading of Chinese text), which rearranges the word order and adds Japanese grammatical particles.

Japanese scholars and poets also composed their own {漢詩|かんし} throughout history, particularly during the Heian and Edo periods.

Do not confuse with the homophone {監視|かんし} (surveillance), which uses different kanji.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {漢詩|かんし}を{詠|よ}む: to compose Chinese poetry
- {漢詩|かんし}を{読|よ}む: to read Chinese poetry
- {唐|とう}の{漢詩|かんし}: Tang dynasty Chinese poetry
